name: Algolaser Alpha MK2 10W
tagline: 10W Entry Alpha MK2: speed-focused open-frame diode
tldr: The 10W Alpha MK2 (often sold as DIY kit or enclosed 10W SKU) is the engraving-first tier. Step up to 20W or 40W for faster fills and deeper cuts.
mainObjective: High-quality hobby and light-business engraving with light, slow cutting

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Algolaser's 10W settings cut 3 mm basswood plywood at 500 mm/min and 6 mm at 200 mm/min, each in one pass
Finest spot of the three tiers in our profile (~0.05 mm): the pick for photo and small-text detail
Low entry price: the DIY KIT MK2 10W was $289 machine-only on Algolaser's store in October 2026
cons: 8–10 mm plywood takes 3 passes on Algolaser's own settings
Black acrylic is slow: 3.5 mm at 100 mm/min, 6 mm in 3 passes
Algolaser sells this tier as the DIY KIT MK2, a separate kit frame from the higher-watt Alpha MK2: compare bundles and assembly before ordering
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 10W SKU on Algolaser Alpha MK2. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run material test grids at engraving speeds first. Add air assist for light cuts. If cut jobs exceed ~30% of your week, open the higher-watt profile on this site and compare times.

editorialDepth.advantages: Algolaser Alpha MK2 10W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Reasonable open-frame entry price.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 5 mm+ cutting in production: see 20W or 40W in the line. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.

faq.question: What does the 10W cut in one pass?
faq.answer: Algolaser's material settings for the DIY KIT MK2 10W list basswood plywood at 500 mm/min (3 mm) and 200 mm/min (5 and 6 mm), in one pass at 100% power. 8 and 10 mm plywood need 3 passes. Black acrylic: 3.5 mm in one pass at 100 mm/min, 6 mm in 3 passes.

faq.question: Which product is the 10W on Algolaser's store?
faq.answer: Algolaser sells its 10W as the DIY KIT MK2: $289 machine-only, $439–659 in kits, or $599 with the smart enclosure (October 2026). The 20W and 40W are sold as the Alpha MK2. Check the work area and accessories on the exact listing, since the kit frame and the Alpha MK2 are different products.

faq.question: Who should choose the 10W over the 20W?
faq.answer: Buyers who engrave far more than they cut. Algolaser's engraving preset for the 10W is 12,000 mm/min on basswood plywood (20,000 on the 20W), and our 10 × 10 cm photo test takes ~14–21 min vs ~9–14 min. If you cut 8 mm stock regularly, the 20W does it in one pass instead of three.

standoutFeatures.title: Finest spot of the line
standoutFeatures.body: ~0.05 mm spot in our profile, the smallest of the three tiers, which helps on photos, small fonts and dense dithering.

standoutFeatures.title: 6 mm plywood in one pass
standoutFeatures.body: Algolaser's own settings cut 5–6 mm basswood plywood in a single pass at 200 mm/min, enough for ornaments, boxes and small signs.

standoutFeatures.title: Low-cost kit option
standoutFeatures.body: $289 machine-only for the DIY KIT MK2 10W in October 2026, the cheapest way into Algolaser's ecosystem.
